messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: NextWave POC – model playbook, benchmarks, and regression guards

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. Below is a concise, action-oriented playbook from our demo that maps recommended model variants to your product constraints (latency target of 250ms p50 for chat, budget ceiling of ~$0.01 per 1k tokens incremental), along with the evaluation artifacts we promised. I focused on candidate models that balance cost, latency, and quality for: short-answer customer support (snippets), multi-turn chat (context up to 2k tokens), and embed+rerank for retrieval.

Recommended shortlist (high level):
- M1-small-quant (approx cost: low, latency: best for 1–2 concurrent workers) — good for high-throughput snippet generation, risk: hallucination rate slightly higher on long-form clarifications; recommended for behind-cache flows.
- M2-standard (approx cost: mid, latency: meets 250ms p50 on dedicated pools) — sweet spot for chat with long context; quality strong across our prompt sets.
- M3-high-qual (approx cost: higher, latency: higher but within budget for reserved capacity) — best for subjective responses and legal/financial tone; use for escalation paths only.

Why these: cost/latency/quality tradeoffs
- M1-small-quant: 40–60% cheaper per token than M3, p50 latency ~120–180ms on your projected request mix with aggressive batching; however output probability mass tends to be concentrated and may miss nuanced phrasing — mitigated by reranking and prompt scaffolding.
- M2-standard: balanced—latency and cost between the two, high pass rate on our quality eval set (see bench CSV), and robust with prefix caching for repeated interactions.
- M3-high-qual: fewer regressions on edge-case prompts (legalese), higher CE (cost) but supports stronger guardrails & structured output.

Evaluation artifacts attached / links:
- Prompt pack (attached: nextwave_prompt_pack_v1.json) — conversation templates, escalation prompts, safety/regression test cases.
- Benchmarks (linked + attached: benchmarks_nextwave_q3.csv) — per-model token cost, latency distributions (p50/p95), and quality metrics (BLEU-like passage-match and custom correctness labels we ran against your sample corpus).
- SLO profile (attached: SLA_latency_profile.pdf) — expected latencies by model on Dedicated vs Hosted tiers; fallback routing recommendations.
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cNextWavePOC (full artifacts + raw eval outputs)

Quality/regression notes (short):
- We saw the largest variance in factuality on long, multi-sentence clarifications with M1; recommend adding a lightweight post-checker + reranker for high-value flows.
- M2 showed consistent behavior across our prompt perturbation sets; M3 is safest for tone-sensitive outputs.

Proposed next steps (pick one):
1) 1-week focused validation sprint (Redwood + NextWave): we run a 5k-sample regression suite (we already have sample IDs) and produce a pass/fail dashboard; estimated 5 working days.
2) Technical Q&A + SLA review (30–45m): deep-dive on latency profiles and integration points (SDKs, KV cache).
3) Pilot config: allocate a small Dedicated pool for M2 + fallback to M1 for high-throughput non-sensitive endpoints.

Can you confirm which option you prefer and whether Samir wants us to include specific SLAs for p95? I’ll circulate the sprint scope and a proposed calendar once you confirm.

Thanks —
Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: nextwave_prompt_pack_v1.json, benchmarks_nextwave_q3.csv, SLA_latency_profile.pdf

Subject: Re: NextWave POC – model playbook, benchmarks, and regression guards

Thanks Tessa — very helpful summary. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side:

1) For the 250ms p50 target, your notes say M2 meets that on a dedicated pool — what are the assumptions about concurrency and batch sizing? Can you share p95 numbers for M2 and M1?
2) For the reranking recommendation on M1, do you have a suggested lightweight reranker (embedding + cosine vs small classifier)? Any rough cost estimate for adding that layer?
3) For the 5k-sample validation sprint, what data do you need from us (sample IDs, expected labels, or anonymized traces)?

Also, Samir asked if Redwood has a recommended default quantization profile for M2 when we run Dedicated (to save cost without impacting QA).

We'd like to pick option (1) — the validation sprint — and we'll aim to provide the sample set by Thursday. Can someone propose an internal schedule/owners?

Best,
Aisha Khan
Head of Product — NextWave AI

- Risk: p95 overshoot under burst concurrency. Mitigation: configure bucketed routing and/or reserved min capacity for critical endpoints.

I'll draft the sprint one-pager and calendar after Karthik and Ben confirm scope.

Aisha / Samir —

Thanks — confirmed: we’ll run option (1) the 5k validation sprint. Quick answers to your questions and what we’ll need: 

1) Latency assumptions (M2): p50 180–240ms, p95 ~420ms on a small Dedicated pool sized for your projected concurrency (est: 8 qps steady, 40 qps bursts). Assumptions: per-request avg 400 tokens, batching window 10ms, GPU instance: A100-equivalent; we’ll surface exact p95 numbers from the bench runs.

2) Reranker approach (M1): start with embedding-based cosine rerank (M-small embeddings) as baseline; classifier reranker as phase 2. Rough incremental cost: adds ~10–18% to total inference cost based on our sample mix; Ben will confirm after infra estimate.

3) Data for sprint: a) list of sample IDs or anonymized traces (preferred); b) expected labels for correctness (if available) or human review budget; c) prioritized flows (critical vs low-value). We can handle anonymized traces and will hash PII client-side if required.

4) Quantization profile (M2): default to 4-bit per-channel quantization with FP16 KV cache if you want cost savings with minimal quality impact. Karthik will include a short AB test plan (M2 full-precision vs 4-bit) in the bench runs.

Next steps: 
- Samir / Aisha to share the 5k sample list by Thu 11/11.
- Karthik & Ben: run bench + reranker scoping in parallel; target internal delivery by EOD Fri 11/12.
- I will share the sprint one-pager + calendar today (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cNextWavePOC).

If you want, we can schedule the technical Q&A (30m) on Friday 11/12 after internal delivery to walk the results together.

Talk soon —
Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
